news.title: Arsenal vs Chelsea: All you need to know
news.body_en: Fourth-placed Chelsea make the short trip north to Emirates Stadium to face an Arsenal team in second place as they defend their first Premier League title in 21 years. Sunday’s kick-off is 4.30pm local time, and a first win there since August 2021 would maintain the west Londoners’ 100 per cent start under Xabi Alonso. The close of the transfer window means the dreamtime is over and every club has the squad that must serve them for the next four months. The first test sees the metropolis’ most successful clubs meet for Chelsea’s second London derby of the season and Arsenal’s first. It hands Morgan Rogers an early chance to validate his preference for the blue half of the capital – he has never previously scored against this weekend’s hosts. This is also the period when the football week starts to fill up – though with no European fixtures, the world champions only have Wednesday’s Carabao Cup visit by Leeds in the midweek calendar. Arsenal’s latest attempt to win the Champions League – a trophy that has so far eluded them – starts at Napoli’s Maradona Stadium on Wednesday. Blues manager Xabi Alonso would love a repeat of his first encounter with the Gunners on his 23rd birthday in November 2004 – a 2-1 victory in which he banged in the opener. Ten years ago a new boss took his promising Chelsea side to Emirates early in the Premier League season. The first half was a write-off as the Blues shipped three without reply, but a tactical switch after the break became a sliding-doors moment. Antonio Conte’s change to a three-man backline led to a thrilling campaign that eventually brought the national title back to west London. That was also one of six seasons when the Blues won away to the defending champions of the Premier League – a 3-0 victory at Claudio Ranieri’s Leicester with Marcos Alonso accounting for two and Pedro the other. The Londoners had done the same against the Premier League’s maiden winners, Manchester Utd – and repeated the feat several times since. Shortly before the 1994 FA Cup final, a Gavin Peacock finish was enough to end United’s 34-game unbeaten home run. Three seasons later, the same opponents were beaten at Old Trafford, with a Michael Duberry header and Luca Vialli’s nutmeg contributing to a 2-1 success. And in December 2001, the Londoners’ dominant display earned a 3-0 victory at United – Mario Melchiot, Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink and Eidur Gudjohnsen finding the net. In April 2010, champions and hosts United were again 2-1 victims – this time Joe Cole and Didier Drogba doing the damage for Carlo Ancelotti’s future title winners. And most recently, in March 2021, Mason Mount’s only goal at Anfield helped topple Liverpool’s crown. Chelsea are aiming to open the season with four successive victories on all fronts for the first time since our title-winning 2016/17 season. With 49 goals from 98 Premier League games, Cole Palmer is one off a half-century – Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink (84) and Diego Costa (85) are the only Blues players to have reached 50 in fewer than 100 matches. Arsenal’s run of nine unbeaten against the Blues in the Premier League is their best since 1995-2005. Xabi Alonso and Mikel Arteta are two of the four current Premier League managers who hail from the Basque region of Spain. (The others are Unai Emery and Andoni Iraola.) The last time Arsenal beat Man City 3-0 in the Community Shield was 2014 – but it was Chelsea who went on to win the Premier League. Chelsea have generated 1.9 or more expected goals before half-time in both league matches to date. The world champions claimed just 26 per cent of possession during last weekend’s 4-3 beating of Brighton – but 53 per cent of total shots (17/32). Joao Pedro has scored and set up goals in both opening league fixtures this season – the first player in the club’s history to do so. Morgan Rogers has created nine chances for team-mates so far this season – the most in the Premier League and the highest total by any Blues player in his first two appearances on record (since 2003/04). Sunday’s match was the 28th we have won 4-3 and the 11th in the Premier League era. Between 9 April 1960 and 4 September 1965, Chelsea won all six league visits to Arsenal’s former ground, Highbury, scoring three or more each time – 4-1, 4-1, 3-0, 4-2, 3-1 and 3-1.

news.title: London's Finest vs The Gunners 🔥
Xabi Alonso backs Reece James to become one of the world's best midfielders
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso knows exactly what it takes to become one of the world's greatest midfielders. So his belief that Chelsea captain Reece James can reach that level carries significant weight. During his playing days, few midfielders could influence games from the middle of the pitch like Alonso. He had an unrivalled range of passing, read the game expertly, and was the orchestrator in teams that won league titles, the Champions League, European Championships, and the World Cup. Naturally, the tactical demands on midfielders have evolved since Alonso hung up his boots in 2017. Yet the qualities and attributes needed to thrive remain similar – and the Chelsea manager believes James has these in abundance. The 26-year-old also brings leadership and connection; James, a boyhood fan, is now into his fourth season as captain. The sight of the England international in the Chelsea midfield is nothing new. It's where he started as we defeated Paris Saint-Germain in the Club World Cup and a position he starred in last term in a game against Arsenal, today's opponents at the Emirates Stadium. And it was before our trip to north London that Alonso was asked whether James, one of the best right-backs in world football, could achieve the same status in midfield. ‘I would say so,' the Blues manager replied. 'He is very comfortable and confident playing in that position. He has the intelligence to play there because, in the middle, you need to be able to connect with your team-mates and know what the best thing to do is before you get the ball. 'He has this awareness. I remember him playing very, very well playing in the middle. So we are using him and he will have a lot of minutes as a midfielder.’ Alonso added: ‘For me, physically, when he is fresh and prepared, he has shown he can compete in the Premier League – no issue. 'As a midfielder, you have to take a lot of easy decisions and many right decisions. You are very connected to the game and are close to the action. Walking is not possible. 'So Reece is very involved in the game and knows where he needs to be. He has the capacity to help the team-mates around him and that is very important to me because he has this presence where he has respect from his teammates. When he says something, they listen and they follow him.' In our opening three matches of the campaign, Alonso has used several different midfield combinations. James was partnered by Lavia against Fulham and then featured alongside Valentin Barco in our Carabao Cup win over Luton Town. Last time out, against Brighton and Hove Albion, James stepped out of the side and it was left to Lavia and Malo Gusto to hold down the middle of the pitch. ‘You plan the squad knowing the profiles you have and some players can play in different positions,' Alonso explained. 'Reece can play in the middle, and Malo Gusto can play in the middle and other positions as well. We look at the squad and feel we are good to go. 'If we have injuries and suspensions, we feel we will be able to manage. So that is why we feel we are in a good position.'

news.title: The Arsenal and Chelsea connections: Who has played for both clubs?
news.body_en: Chelsea versus Arsenal is a London derby which first took place in 1907 so it will come as no surprise that quite a few players have featured for both teams over the years. Here we look at some of those to have worn the blue and red during the Premier League era. To qualify for this list, a player must have made a competitive senior appearance for both clubs and must no longer play for either. That excludes current Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martinez, as well as Arsenal trio Kepa Arrizabalaga, Kai Havertz and Noni Madueke. Cech is a certified Chelsea legend, having played for the club between 2004 and 2015. He won four Premier Leagues, four FA Cups, three League Cups, and both the Champions League and Europa League. The former Czechia international is widely considered to be one of the greatest goalkeepers of his generation and after transferring to Arsenal in 2015, he became a fans' favourite at the Emirates too during his final four seasons as a player, whilst also adding an FA Cup to his collection. Cech returned to the Bridge in 2019 and for three years worked as our technical and performance advisor, providing guidance and support on all football matters throughout the club. The Brazilian defender enjoyed two stints in SW6, from 2011 to 2014 and then again from 2016 to 2019. The charismatic and ball-playing centre-back was a hit both on the pitch and off it at the Blues, winning the Champions League, two Europa Leagues, the Premier League and two FA Cups. Luiz joined Arsenal in 2019 and played in north London for two seasons, where he also added another FA Cup medal to his trophy cabinet. Gallas proved to be an excellent bit of business for Chelsea as the young defender would go on to become an integral part of the Blues side which won two Premier Leagues and a League Cup during his five years at the Bridge. Quick, strong, defensively sound and good on the ball, Gallas' quality meant he forged impressive partnerships with Marcel Desailly and John Terry when used in his preferred position of centre-back. But his outstanding versatility meant he was equally adept at playing right-back or left-back, where he spent much of his time during our 2004/05 title win. Gallas was part of the deal which brought Ashley Cole to Stamford Bridge and the France international would play regularly for the Gunners during his four years at the club, before making the move to north London rivals Tottenham. The legendary left-back made his senior debut for Arsenal in 1999 and remained at the Gunners until 2006, winning three FA Cups and two Premier League titles in that time. Cole's standing as one of - and in some fans' eyes the - best left-back in English football history grew even further at Chelsea. Good in defence and attack, with the speed to handle any winger, Cole won the Champions League, Europa League, Premier League, four FA Cups and the League Cup during his time at Stamford Bridge. The fact only five clubs have won more FA Cups than Cole's seven in the competition's 150-plus-year history says a lot about his quality and he is rightly revered as one of the greatest left-backs of all time. The holding midfielder first made his mark in professional football at Le Havre before signing for Chelsea in 2005. The France international spent two seasons at the Bridge, winning both domestic cups in that time. He then moved to Arsenal in August 2007 before joining Portsmouth the following January, having even more success at Real Madrid and several other clubs. Petit joined Arsenal from French side Monaco in 1997 and spent three seasons at the club, winning the Premier League and FA Cup with the Gunners while also lifting the World Cup and European Championship with France. After spending the next season at Barcelona, the Frenchman returned to the English capital in 2001 to join the Blues. Petit spent three years at the Bridge but unfortunately had to retire through knee injury six months after leaving the Blues. A true Arsenal legend, Rocastle was an integral part of the Gunners team which won the First Division - now the Premier League - title in 1989 and 1991. After spells at high-flying Leeds United and then Manchester City, former Blues manager Glenn Hoddle brought 'Rocky' to Stamford Bridge in 1994 and the midfielder was still able to make an impact during his initial couple of years at the club, despite having to manage knee injuries. Rocastle sadly passed away at the age of just 33 in 2001 due to non-Hodgkin lymphoma but his infectious personality, quality on the pitch and outstanding 'one-for-all' mentality mean his name is still sung from the Emirates stands even to this day. Little was known about Fabregas when he moved to Arsenal as a teenager but he would become one of the best centre midfielders of the Premier League era and a serial winner. Fabregas may have only lifted one FA Cup during his eight years at Arsenal but he was a key part of the Gunners team which reached the Champions League final and his talent took him back to Barcelona, where he enjoyed a trophy-laden three years. A switch to Chelsea in 2014 saw the trophies keep coming as he played a big part in us winning two Premier Leagues, one FA Cup and a League Cup before departing for Monaco five years later. Benayoun joined Chelsea in 2010 after successful spells at the likes of West Ham United and Liverpool. The attacking midfielder struggled to cement a regular spot at Chelsea during his three years at the club but still managed to claim a Europa League winner's medal in 2013. Although he spent longer at the Bridge, Benayoun actually played more games for Arsenal during his one-season loan at the Gunners in the 2011/12 campaign. Willian enjoyed a hugely influential seven years at Chelsea between 2013 and 2020, lifting the Europa League, two Premier Leagues, one FA Cup and one League Cup while at the Bridge. The manner of his arrival at Chelsea, not to mention his performances while in Blue, means his name is still sung in the stands at Stamford Bridge. Willian spent a season at Arsenal following his departure from Chelsea and after a year back in his native Brazil, returned to the Premier League and West London for two successful seasons with Fulham before joining Olympiacos in the summer of 2024. A second spell at Fulham and a stint back in Brazil with Gremio since followed, before he left the side in the summer of 2026. The striker burst on to the Premier League scene following his move to Arsenal while still 17 years old and quickly established himself as one of the most exciting talents in Europe. After helping the Gunners to the league and cup double in 1998 and claiming the Premier League's Golden Boot the following season, he made a big-money move to Real Madrid and re-joined Paris Saint-Germain before returning to the Premier League with a loan to Liverpool in 2001. Further spells at English sides and in Turkey were to follow before Anelka joined Chelsea in January 2008, and helped the Blues reach the Champions League final later that season. An FA Cup winner's medal arrived the next season, when he was included in the Premier League Team of the Year, before Anelka played a big part in us winning the Premier League and FA Cup double in 2010. Giroud joined Arsenal in 2012 from Montpellier under Arsene Wenger and spent six years in north London, winning three FA Cups in that time. A switch to Chelsea in January 2018 was quickly followed by the striker winning another FA Cup with the Blues and him playing a huge role in France lifting the World Cup that summer. Giroud would then go on to claim the Golden Boot as Chelsea won the Europa League in 2019 and he scored six goals in eight games on our way to winning the Champions League two years later. Aubameyang had already established himself as one of European football's top marksmen by the time he arrived in London and that status was just reinforced during his years in the capital. The Gabon international scored 92 goals in 163 games during his four years at Arsenal, which included claiming the Premier League Golden Boot in the 2018/19 season and he was named the club's Player of the Year the following campaign, when his 29 goals included braces against Manchester City and Chelsea in the FA Cup semi-final and final respectively. A seven-month stint at Barcelona, where he picked up a La Liga's winner's medal, came to an end when he joined Chelsea in September 2022. The forward would score three goals in 23 outings in his season at the Blues before heading off for two successful spells with Marseille, either side of a stint in Saudi Arabia with Al-Qadsiah, and is now at Deportivo La Coruna. The Italy international arrived at Stamford Bridge from Napoli in the summer of 2018 and became an integral member of the Chelsea teams that won several continental trophies, including the 2021 Champions League in Porto. In total the midfielder made over 200 appearances for us, scoring 29 goals - of which many were ice-cool penalties - before heading to Arsenal in January 2023. In the summer of 2025, after two-and-a-half seasons at the Emirates, Jorginho returned to Brazil, the country of his birth, to play for Flamengo. The England international joined Chelsea in the summer of 2022 and was a regular during his first two seasons at the club, making 81 appearances and scoring 19 goals. Sterling then joined Arsenal on loan for the 2024/25 campaign where he scored one goal in 28 outings in all competitions. The 31-year-old departed Chelsea in January 2026 by mutual agreement and spent the second half of the season at Feyenoord.

news.title: Chelsea's most memorable meetings with Arsenal
news.body_en: Chelsea's history is intertwined with that of London’s longest-running top-flight derby match, with the next instalment awaiting us on Sunday. Over our 121 years, the Blues have met Arsenal, our rivals from across the capital, on more than 200 occasions across six different competitions. But before the latest chapter in the storied rivalry is written, we recite some of our favourite passages from the 119-year-long history of Chelsea vs Arsenal. The first-ever meeting between Chelsea and Woolwich Arsenal – as our opponents were then known – arrived two years after the former club was formed. What was then a record league crowd in the capital witnessed Chelsea draw first blood in this rivalry, thanks to two strikes by the legendary striker George Hilsdon. Goals in the 13th and 77th minutes meant Charlie Satterthwaite’s reply for the visitors was a mere consolation. This new derby made quite an impression on the locals too, with the London-based Morning Leader newspaper glimpsing the future by declaring: ‘This great game will be fought over again a thousand times in the family circle, in club, workshop, office and factory.’ The crowd from that first meeting between Chelsea and Arsenal was comfortably surpassed at this draw in 1935, which remains the largest officially recorded attendance for any match at Stamford Bridge. A raucous 82,905 people crammed into the Bridge to see the two sides, separated by just two points in the top-flight table at the time, go head-to-head. Managed by Leslie Knighton and captained by one-club man Tommy Law, the Chelsea side featured Dicky Spence, who would go on to score a record 19 goals in this fixture across 14 years, in blue. Unfortunately the huge number of Chelsea supporters in attendance didn’t get to celebrate a victory, as Joe Bambrick’s second-half goal for the home side was cancelled out by a Jack Crayston equaliser for Arsenal. It may seem strange to include a second draw on our list, but this visit to Highbury for our opening game of the 1984/85 campaign was a pivotal moment in the club’s history. A painful five-year absence from the top division – during which the club’s very existence came under threat – had come to an end, and our return began with a tough trip to an Arsenal side well-established in the upper reaches of the table. So big was the excitement among the Blues faithful that there were large numbers of Chelsea supporters visible in all four corners of Arsenal’s stadium. And a Kerry Dixon equaliser sparked wild celebrations and earned a draw that proved we were back where we belonged and able to compete with the top teams in the country again. We have played outside the top flight for just one season since. Chelsea’s first-ever appearance in the last four of European football’s most prestigious competition arrived in 2004, courtesy of a dramatic win over Arsenal. A 1-1 draw in the first leg at Stamford Bridge had given the Gunners the advantage, and a Jose Antonio Reyes goal at Highbury extended further. That left us with 45 minutes to score twice without reply in order to continue our European journey. We were given hope when Frank Lampard made it 2-2 on aggregate just six minutes into the second half; he slotted home a rebound after Jens Lehmann couldn’t hold Claude Makelele’s powerful drive. That set up a tense finale, which was settled from an unlikely source, as full-back Wayne Bridge raced onto Eidur Gudjohnsen’s pass in the 87th minute to fire Chelsea into the Champions League semi-finals for the first time. It may not have been pretty, but this win represented a shift in the balance of power in London and English football. Despite claiming our first top-flight title for 50 years a few months earlier, our hoodoo against the Gunners persisted until Didier Drogba’s second-half strike ended a run of 20 league games without a win for the Blues in this fixture. Drogba had netted two excellent goals in a 2-1 Community Shield win over the same opponents two weeks earlier, but this time, on our second game of the campaign, he bundled the ball past the keeper with his knee while attempting to control Lampard's pass. Not that any of the home fans at the Bridge cared how it went in, as it was our first winning league goal against Arsenal after 20 attempts. In quite a turnaround, we would go on to win 11 of the next 20 Premier League meetings. Drogba was something of a nemesis for Arsenal during his time with Chelsea, and never looked more at home than he did on the big stage at Wembley Stadium. Both of those traits were on show in this FA Cup semi-final. We had initially fallen behind to Theo Walcott’s goal following a strong start by the Gunners, before Florent Malouda levelled things up shortly after the half-hour mark with an excellent strike, cutting onto his left foot and beating the keeper at his near post. As was so often the case, though, it was Drogba who proved decisive, pouncing to settle the game with six minutes remaining. He put Arsenal to the sword when he brushed aside Mikael Silvestre to latch on to Lampard’s long ball, round Lukasz Fabianski and slot the winner into an empty net. We would return to the national stadium to lift the famous old trophy by beating Everton in the final. Chelsea’s biggest-ever win over Arsenal came at just about the most painful time possible for the Gunners, as long-serving manager Arsene Wenger marked his 1,000th game in charge. Perhaps they should have seen it coming, having lost on five of their six previous visits to Stamford Bridge. By the time Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain was sent off in a case of mistaken identity after Kieran Gibbs had handled on the line, Chelsea were already two up through Samuel Eto’o and Andre Schurrle. Eden Hazard’s penalty then made it 3-0 inside 20 minutes. The game was already all but over, but we rubbed salt into the wound as Oscar found the net twice before Mohamed Salah completed the record 6-0 scoreline. It left Wenger with nothing to smile about on his landmark day. For many, Eden Hazard was the dominant figure of this era in Chelsea’s history, and this game featured what was perhaps the defining goal of the brilliant Belgian’s time at Stamford Bridge. Marcos Alonso gave us the lead before the break, and shortly after it, Hazard demonstrated all the balance, close control, skills and composure that made him such a special player. Picking up possession in his own half, Eden left a trail of Arsenal players sprawled in his wake as he charged into the area and lifted a deft finish over his former Blues team-mate Petr Cech. Cesc Fabregas and Olivier Giroud would score against their former and future clubs late on, but it was Hazard’s goal that effectively made the points safe for Chelsea – and they turned out to be an important three points in our successful pursuit of a sixth league championship. In 2019 victory over Arsenal ended with Chelsea captain Cesar Azpilicueta lifting a trophy – namely the Europa League after our second appearance in the final in Baku. This time, Giroud netted for Chelsea against Arsenal, with a superb header shortly after half-time, to seal his status as the competition’s top scorer. That was the first of four Blues goals scored past Cech – making his last appearance before retirement – in the space of 23 minutes which left our opponents well beaten. Hazard again proved too good for the Gunners, setting up Pedro for our second, converting a penalty for the third, and sweeping in the fourth after combining brilliantly with Giroud, leaving Alex Iwobi’s strike in reply meaningless. It was quite a way for Hazard to sign off in his final game for Chelsea.

news.title: What kit are Chelsea wearing against Arsenal?
news.body_en: Another London derby awaits Xabi Alonso and his Chelsea players tomorrow as the Blues make a short journey across the capital to face Arsenal. Our top-flight campaign has started with back-to-back victories. We overcame Fulham at Craven Cottage in our season opener and saw off Brighton and Hove Albion at Stamford Bridge last weekend. Arsenal will pose a different challenge. The Gunners have also started the season with consecutive victories and have done so without conceding a goal. Yet no team has scored more than the Blues thus far, with our front three of Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers in fine form. And that trio, alongside their Blues team-mates, will walk out at the Emirates Stadium wearing our 2026/27 Nike home kit. The 'Bright Blue' shirt has our refreshed club crest interwoven into the fabric and features a button-down neck and 'Midwest Gold' accents for the rampant lion badge and Nike swoosh. It celebrates the 75th season since Ted Drake took over as Chelsea manager and reshaped the club’s identity, replacing our Pensioners nickname with the Blues and introducing our now-iconic lion symbol. Click here to purchase your Chelsea home shirt!

news.title: Internationals: Four Blues help England to earn a point at the Women's Under-20 World Cup
news.body_en: There was late drama as an England side that featured four Blues across the 90 minutes needed a late penalty to secure a draw against Canada in their opening match at the FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup. The tournament features 24 teams and runs from 5 to 27 September. England WU20 head coach Lydia Bedford selected Chelsea's Katie Cox in goal, with fellow Blues Lola Brown and Vera Jones also named in the starting line-up. Two more young Blues, Chloe Sarwie and Eva Hendle, were named among the substitutes. The Lionesses fell behind just after half-time, when English-born Annabelle Chukwu netted for the Canadians. Brown was switched for Sarwie in the second half, and with five minutes remaining, England still trailed by a goal. England’s fortunes changed in the closing stages when they were awarded a penalty. The responsibility fell to Aston Villa's Rachel Maltby to take the spot-kick, and she showed no nerves in helping England take a point after 89 minutes. England take on Tanzania on Tuesday 8 September at 5pm and Brazil on Friday 11 September at 2pm in their remaining Group B fixtures, which will all take place in Bielsko-Biala.After the group stage, the tournament progresses to the knockout rounds and the Women's U-20 World Cup final will be played in Lodz on Sunday 27 September.

news.title: WSL Highlights: Chelsea 1-1 Aston Villa
WSL Full Match: Chelsea vs Aston Villa
How Morgan Rogers has fulfilled Xabi Alonso's expectations at Chelsea
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso admits he is a little surprised at Morgan Rogers' immediate impact at Chelsea, but believes it justifies why the England international was 'the number one target' for the Blues this summer. After helping England to a third-place finish at this summer's World Cup, Rogers completed a move to Stamford Bridge from Aston Villa. Yet it wasn't until 11 August, after a deserved holiday, that he began training with his new team-mates. A pre-season outing against Real Sociedad, in which he scored, was Rogers' only game time before our Premier League campaign got underway. Yet there was no indication of the 24-year-old being undercooked on his debut at Craven Cottage. Rogers opened his account for the Blues with a well-taken, first-half strike as we went on to win 3-2 at our west London neighbours Fulham. The following weekend against Brighton and Hove Albion at Stamford Bridge, he produced an excellent assist for Pedro Neto to score. Rogers will look to maintain his strong start at Chelsea on Sunday when we make the short trip across London to take on Arsenal. And ahead of that fixture, Alonso was asked whether Rogers' instantaneous impact had surprised him. He replied: 'Probably yes, because it’s been just three weeks since he started playing for Chelsea, started training with us and getting his fitness level, but he has had a very good impact. 'I hoped he would have a straight impact on the team and that he would get along with his team-mates so well, because he knew many of them. That’s why he was such an important target and a goal for us to get him, and once we got him in the building, he fulfilled our expectations.' Rogers' signing was one of many the Blues made this summer, with the squad reshaped following Alonso's appointment as manager ahead of the 2026/27 campaign. Quality and experience – in different forms – were added to the group, yet Alonso says that the skillset that Rogers provides made him an important addition. 'He was the number one target for us,' the Spaniard said. 'Talking about squad planning, taking big decisions, for sure, Morgan was a big one as we get a player of his stature in the present and for the future. 'He will be a key player for the next six, seven years. Right now, he has had a great impact and his chemistry with the whole team is great, and the chemistry with his strike partners is fantastic. 'That's happening in such a short time. It gives us a lot of hope for the future – and he looks really happy as well, which is important.'

news.title: Bronze's post-Aston Villa thoughts
Sonia reflects on Aston Villa draw
Sonia Bompastor gives Malard injury update and rues missed chances
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor explained why striker Melvine Malard was absent from the squad this afternoon and why our finishing was not enough to kill off the game as we drew 1-1 with Aston Villa at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Saturday's clash with Aston Villa saw us take the lead after 11 minutes through Lauren James, but after our 34 shots on goal, we could not add to the lead, and the visitors scored an equaliser with 10 minutes to play. Our new No.9 Malard scored a brace in our 5-2 win over Real Sociedad at Plough Lane in our first competitive match of the campaign but was absent for the second leg of that tie and again today. 'Melvine picked up a knock in training, so she should be back soon,' Bompastor confirmed. 'But at the same time, it's difficult to have a more precise timeframe for her return. For sure, if you have more availability in the squad with some profiles, it always helps. 'I didn't have a number nine on the bench today, someone who plays in that position and has a lot of experience, so that's the reality. But today, for me, if you analyse the game and the performance, we created enough chances to be able to score in different ways. 'Many players in the squad had the opportunity to score. The goalkeeper had a really good game. She made a lot of big saves. That's the reality. But I still think we could've done better with some of the chances we created.' Aston Villa's debutant goalkeeper Akane Okuma made a series of fine saves throughout the match, and Keira Walsh had her brilliant effort bounce down off the underside of the crossbar and out again. Yet Bompastor wasn't looking for excuses as she explained the areas in which she wants the team to improve. 'If you analyse the performance today and the statistics of the game, you could say it's crazy we didn't win the game,' she said. 'We created a lot of opportunities. 'The reality of football is that in this kind of game, we need to be two or three-nil up by half-time, and the game is over. Then, it's a completely different game coming into the second half because when you have two or three goals difference, you can bring players in, rotate the squad. 'Being only one-nil up, you can always be exposed, so you try to find the balance between keeping the attacking style, but also avoiding the transition and the situations for Villa. So we focused a lot on that in the second half, but it was not enough. 'In terms of mentality and mindset, I spoke before the game about the fact that when you play these games, a one-nil lead is not enough. You need to keep the momentum. You need to speed up the game as quickly as possible, and you need to sustain that. You need to make sure you accelerate to kill the game because when you are only one-nil up, you don't kill the opposition. 'So that's what happened today, and at the end of the game, we were all frustrated because it's not a good result, and I think we had the opportunity today to win the game, kill the game, and many more things.'

news.title: Aggie Beever-Jones reaches 100 appearances for Chelsea
news.body_en: Aggie Beever-Jones reached a significant Chelsea milestone this afternoon, as she made her 100th appearance for the Blues in our 1-1 draw against Aston Villa. The striker joined the Chelsea Academy at nine years old and signed her first professional contract in July 2021, on the day she turned 18. Beever-Jones made her Blues debut against Aston Villa in January 2021 and now comes full circle as she completes her 100th Chelsea appearance, facing the same opponent today at Stamford Bridge. Scoring for the first time in blue against Brighton and Hove Albion in 2023, she now has 32 Chelsea goals to her name over 100 outings. She has celebrated consistent success at Chelsea, winning the Women's Super League twice and lifting both the Women’s FA Cup and Women’s League Cup on two occasions. Last season, she scored on the opening day of the campaign in our 2-1 win against Manchester City and netted our second goal as we beat Manchester United 2-0 to lift the Women's League Cup trophy in consecutive seasons. Those performances caught the eye of England head coach Sarina Wiegman, and the Chelsea Academy graduate made her first senior start for England in May 2025. She announced herself on the international stage in style, netting a 30-minute hat-trick against Portugal in the Women’s Nations League at Wembley Stadium. She was also included in the 23-player squad for the 2025 Women’s European Championship. Beever-Jones scored in England’s 6-1 win over Wales in the competition’s group stage before going on to lift the trophy with five of her Chelsea team-mates. Extending her contract in July this year, Aggie will remain with Chelsea until at least 2030.

news.title: Under-18 Premier League report: Fulham 4-3 Chelsea
news.body_en: Chelsea were beaten 4-3 by Fulham in the Under-18 Premier League after an impressive fightback from our London rivals. The Blues were in control for much of the first half and deservedly led 2-0 as we moved towards half-time thanks to goals from Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli and Chizaram Ezenwata, with Fulham goalkeeper Zack Brief making several other saves to keep his side in the contest. However, Leo Hamilton reduced the deficit in first-half injury time and Fulham struck twice early in the second half to move ahead. Ezenwata’s penalty brought Chelsea level with 14 minutes remaining but Tarrell Cavell’s second goal of the game then decided the contest. Heze Grimwade had the first opportunity after eight minutes, dragging a right-footed effort wide from the centre of the box. Chelsea went ahead five minutes later. Nicoll-Jazuli tried twice from a tight angle before converting at the third attempt from close range. Ezenwata almost doubled our advantage immediately when his drive from outside the box was tipped over by Brief, before Nicoll-Jazuli struck the right post. The second goal arrived in the 20th minute. Richards played the ball down the line to Jashayde Greenwood, whose square pass left Ezenwata with a simple finish. Brief denied Greenwood with a fine save from a shot heading towards the top corner and then rushed from his goal to stop Grimwade following a slick Chelsea move. Calvin Diakite made an important challenge at the other end after Fulham capitalised on a loose pass, but the hosts pulled one back in first-half injury time when Hamilton finished from around eight yards. Richards tested Brief from distance shortly after the restart, while Isaac Collinson made an excellent save at the other end before the rebound struck the crossbar. The hosts equalised in the 51st minute through Aidan Evans, who found the top corner. Cavell then put Fulham ahead for the first time five minutes later with another well-taken strike from outside the box. Chelsea continued to create openings. Ezenwata curled narrowly over, Greenwood sent two efforts off target and substitute Eden Mahoney-Smith was also close with a curling attempt. The Blues drew level in the 76th minute. After Ibrahim Rabbaj had seen a shot saved, Ezenwata found Nicoll-Jazuli, who was brought down inside the box. Ezenwata stepped forward and drove the resulting penalty into the corner. Cavell restored Fulham’s advantage six minutes later, though, meeting a cross from the right with a first-time finish. Nicoll-Jazuli and Greenwood had late efforts as Chelsea searched for another equaliser, before Lewi Richards received his second booking and a red card in the seventh minute of added time. The result leaves Chelsea eighth in the Under-18 Premier League table with six points from four matches. Fulham are second with 10 points from their opening four fixtures. news.title: Match Report: Chelsea 1-1 Aston Villa
news.body_en: A stunning opening goal from Lauren James was cancelled out by an unfortunate own goal from Veerle Buurman as we dominated Aston Villa at Stamford Bridge but only came away with a point. The Blues began with an aggressive start, pressing high and firing shots towards the Aston Villa goal. And our approach paid off when we won the ball back high up the pitch, Ellie Carpenter picking out James with a pass before the no. 10 opened our account with an emphatic finish high into the net from the left-hand side. Multiple chances followed in the second half, the best of which saw Keira Walsh desperately unlucky not to score a wonder goal from outside of the area, but she was thwarted by the finest of margins when the ball bounced out off the underside of the bar. Villa scored with one of their three shots on target when the ball pinged around the penalty area and took an unlucky bounce off Buurman, giving us just ten minutes to find a response. Only a fantastic save from the visiting goalkeeper kept James from netting her second, leaving us with only a point from our opening WSL match of the campaign. Sonia Bompastor took the opportunity to rotate her side after our midweek trip to face Real Sociedad, bringing Buurman, Sjoeke Nusken, Katie McCabe and Alyssa Thompson into the starting XI in place of Naomi Girma, Kadeisha Buchanan, Sandy Baltimore and Lexi Potter, who all began the match on the substitutes' bench. The Blues were lively right from the start, and with only three minutes on the clock, Lauren James dribbled the ball into space in the penalty area before pulling her shot just wide of the left-hand post. On her 100th appearance for Chelsea, Aggie Beever-Jones then tried a clever backheeled attempt close to the goalkeeper, which didn't quite come off. Then, after some neat passing around the box, Lucy Bronze responded to the shouts of 'shoot' from outside the penalty area and forced a fingertip save from Akane Okuma as the attempt went over the bar. As our visitors opted to play the ball out from the back, the Blues sprang into action with an intense press, allowing Ellie Carpenter to win the ball back high up the pitch. Feeding the ball to James, our number 10 dribbled towards goal on the left-hand side before she unleashed a wicked left-footed shot from a tight angle into the back of the net. It was a moment of sublime individual skill, but also a just reward for the way in which we had started the match. Beever-Jones then showed real vision to spot an opportunity to beat the goalkeeper when she attempted an audacious chip from the left corner of the box, only to see her attempt fly just over the top-right corner of the crossbar. The match settled into a rhythm as Chelsea's initial ruthless intensity dropped slightly, but we had a couple more chances to add to the scoreline before the interval when Thompson's shot went just wide of the far post, and Wieke Kaptein saw her attempt blocked by a superb tackle near the goal line. In the second half, the Blues remained in control. After an hour, we had taken 40 touches in the Villa penalty area as opposed to their two touches in ours. We looked to add to the lead when a well-worked set piece 40 yards from goal fashioned a chance for James to shoot from outside the box, but this time her attempt went high of the target. Carpenter then fired a powerful shot on goal, which Okuma did well to tip round the post, and the goalkeeper was on hand once more to gather an effort from Beever-Jones. Next to try her luck was Walsh, and after scoring from range in midweek against Real Sociedad, she blasted a shot with such ferocity that the ball bounced down off the underside of the crossbar and away from danger with the goalkeeper already beaten. We continued to press hard for our second goal of the afternoon. James played a wonderful crossfield ball to Carpenter, who contorted her body to get her shot away before the attempt trickled wide. Then McCabe, who had been dangerous all afternoon, put a pinpoint cross into the far post and Beever-Jones had the ball in the net, only to be judged as offside. After so much domination, one moment from Villa changed the look of the contest. As the ball pinged around the box, an unlucky ricochet off Buurman took the ball over Hannah Hampton and across the line to level the scores with only 10 minutes to play. The Blues fought hard, and when Lucy Bronze played in a dangerous cross, only a fantastic save from Okuma could keep James from scoring her second of the afternoon. This was a good performance from Chelsea with 60 entries into the final third, 57 touches in the opposition box and 34 shots on goal. A little bit of luck and some clinical finishing was lacking on the day, as Villa's debutant goalkeeper pulled off some excellent saves. We move forward to Manchester United with plenty of positives to take from our opening league match. We kick off our 2026/27 WSL campaign with a point on the board. We head north to face Manchester United in the WSL next Sunday, with kick-off set for noon. news.title: Confirmed Chelsea Women line up vs Aston Villa
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has made four changes to her Chelsea side for our first Women's Super League match of the season against Aston Villa. After the midweek win over Real Sociedad, Bompastor explained she was delighted to utilise some of the younger members of the squad during the 1-0 victory. And having rotated on Wednesday, the head coach now makes four changes to her starting line-up, bringing Veerle Buurman into the defence with summer signing Katie McCabe, who makes her first appearance at Stamford Bridge as a Chelsea player today. Sjoeke Nusken comes back into the midfield alongside Keira Walsh as Chelsea Academy graduate Lexi Potter is named on the bench. Alyssa Thompson is back in the starting XI to spearhead the attack. Aggie Beever-Jones, who signed a contract extension until 2030 this summer, makes her 100th appearance for the Blues in our first match at the Bridge since it was made our permanent home. news.title: Alonso highlights the 'quality and competitiveness' of his midfield options
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso believes he has the midfield options to adapt to the different challenges Chelsea will face in the Premier League and keep his players fresh through the season. The Blues manager has already used several midfield combinations in the opening three matches of his tenure, all of which ended in victory. That has seen Valentin Barco, Romeo Lavia, Malo Gusto and Reece James all start in midfield, while Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson will also be options Alonso can turn to once they are back to full fitness. Combined with the young talent coming through the ranks of the Chelsea Academy, with the likes of teenagers Reggie Watson and Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli featuring during pre-season, Alonso is pleased with the options available to him in the weeks and months ahead. ‘We have different qualities and personalities,’ he said. ‘Players like Valentin – he's young but has come with great energy. ‘We have Hendo who has the composure, the mentality. He knows what's going on in the game, and he's getting closer and closer to playing time. ‘And with Rom, Moi, Reece, Malo can play there, Watson as well, Mahdi from the Academy, we have options. We need to have the right balance and within that we have quality and competitiveness for all the season and to face each opponent.’ Those players will also enable Alonso to rotate his midfield as form and fitness dictates, something he hopes will help keep energy levels high throughout the season. ‘I think that this year, knowing that we won't have as many games, we are able to manage more minutes, to spread them around and to have a proper distribution depending on the games, depending on the momentum of each player,’ continued Alonso. ‘Hopefully, touch wood, they don't have that many setbacks because that's what you want from players, and especially from Rom, that he is feeling better, that we need to push him to have this consistency in his fitness level.’ We will have to wait until Sunday to find out which of those options Alonso chooses to use against the title holders Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.
